Private Sub Dress(ByVal which As Long, c As Object)
    Select Case which
    Case 0: c.SeriesCollection(2).Trendlines.Add
    Case 1: c.SeriesCollection(1).Trendlines.Add: c.SeriesCollection(2).Trendlines.Add
    Case 2: c.SeriesCollection(1).Trendlines.Add: c.SeriesCollection(1).Trendlines.Add
    Case 3: c.Legend.Left = 10
    End Select
End Sub
Private Sub Edit(ByVal which As Long, c As Object, r As Variant)
    Select Case which
    Case 1: c.SeriesCollection(1).Points(1).HasDataLabel = True: r = c.SeriesCollection(1).Points(1).HasDataLabel
    Case 2: c.SeriesCollection(1).Points(1).Format.Fill.ForeColor.RGB = 255: r = c.SeriesCollection(1).Points(1).Format.Fill.ForeColor.RGB
    Case 3: c.SeriesCollection.NewSeries: r = c.SeriesCollection.Count
    End Select
End Sub

Public Function Make(ByVal path As String, ByVal which As Long) As String
    Dim wb As Workbook, ws As Worksheet, c As Object
    Set wb = Workbooks.Add(xlWBATWorksheet)
    Set ws = wb.Worksheets(1)
    ws.Name = "One"
    ws.Range("A1:C1").Value = Array("", "Rev", "Cost")
    ws.Range("A2:C2").Value = Array("a", 10, 4)
    ws.Range("A3:C3").Value = Array("b", 20, 6)
    Set c = ws.ChartObjects.Add(48, 96, 240, 144).Chart
    c.SetSourceData ws.Range("A1:C3")
    Dress which, c
    wb.SaveAs path, xlOpenXMLWorkbook
    wb.Close False
End Function

Public Function Act(ByVal path As String, ByVal out As String, ByVal which As Long) As String
    Dim wb As Workbook, c As Object, r As Variant, s As String
    Set wb = Workbooks.Open(path)
    Set c = wb.Worksheets(1).ChartObjects(1).Chart
    On Error Resume Next
    Edit which, c, r
    s = Err.Number & " " & TypeName(r) & " " & r
    On Error GoTo 0
    Application.DisplayAlerts = False
    wb.SaveAs out, xlOpenXMLWorkbook
    Application.DisplayAlerts = True
    wb.Close False
    Act = s
End Function
